summary: Rutherford County lookout: a wooden tower was replaced in 1934 by a 47 ft 9 in steel tower built with ECW funding; no source describes its later fate.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: A wooden tower was replaced by a 47-foot 9-inch steel tower using ECW funding.

evidence.supports: The lookout is in Rutherford County and the page names the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources as the agency.
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: A statewide list of the North Carolina lookouts gives the county and agency.
evidence.quote: Rutherford County - North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: In 1934 the wooden tower was replaced with a 47-foot 9-inch steel tower using ECW funding.
evidence.quote: 1934: The wooden tower was replaced with a 47-foot 9-inch steel tower using ECW funding.

evidence.supports: The page cites the Department of Conservation and Development's 5th biennial report for 1932-34 for this detail.
evidence.quote: Department of Conservation and Development - 5th Biennial Report 1932-34

evidence.supports: A statewide tower list places Biggerstaff Mountain in Rutherford County at 35.5 north and 81.82083 west.

corrections.why: The lookout page gives 47 feet 9 inches, about 14.55 m. The brief's 14.3 m matches 47 feet alone and drops the 9 inches.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one detailed line on the lookout page, cited to a 1932-34 state report, plus the county and agency lines on the state list. Brief status and access were unknown and no source gives either, so they are left out and the story says so for today. Staffing and fires are not in any source found. The brief's height of 14.3 m is corrected to 14.6 m (47 ft 9 in). The page's 'ECW' abbreviation is kept as printed. A Facebook group question refers to the Biggerstaff tower in the past tense; it is not a source and is not cited. No photos found.
